It all depends on your philosophy of use.

If you're buying a firearm with the sole expectation being that you'll use it to defend yourself, or otherwise only shoot at humans - then yes, something purposefully anti-personnel like a handgun or an AR15 would do.

The reason I recommend shotguns is because they are:

  • A versatile starting firearm. Capable of firing everything from Dust Shot to 1oz slugs.

  • 12ga ammunition is cheap, plentiful and ubiquitous, compared to any other calibre. And again, it can be loaded with a wide variety of projectiles.

  • They are more public and media-friendly. A wood and steel shotgun has associations of hunting, sports, pioneer and outdoor culture. They are the least intimidating of firearms. Leading to...

  • They are often the last firearms to fall to gun control. It's hard to make excuses to take away shotguns from people using them for animal defence, recreational shooting, family heirloom, etc.

By all means, if you can, get all of those - rifle, pistol, shotgun. But be realistic as to your philosophy of use and what you intend to get guns for.

They are tools. Not talismans. Simply owning a firearm won't protect you. A weapon you don't know how to use belongs to your enemy.

When selecting your first firearm, factor in ammunition cost and availability. Ideally over the life of a gun, you will spend more on ammo than you did on the firearm. Because you should be practicing.

Practicing drawing, dry firing, sighting, live fire, moving and firing, clearing structure interiors. These are all important skills if you want to get the benefit of a firearm as a safety and protection tool.

Also, Pistol shooting is a lot more difficult than the movies make it look. They are inherent less accurate and far less powerful than a rifle. Their only real advantage is size and hence, concealability.

Ultimately, the answer is to own multiple firearms; each suited to particular needs and circumstances. One thing to be aware of is the political climate. In which case, buying an AR would be a prudent idea. Just remember that the expenditure should also include: ammo, magazines, accessories (such as optics, sights or handling addons), and most importantly a way to carry it all - such as rifle slings and ammo carriers/chest rigs.

Firearm ownership is a deep, expensive hole to fall down, but a rewarding one. You're fortunate to live in the United States where sound firearm laws are enshrined in legislation. Take advantage of that while it lasts.
